pairs: Et eduxit me in atrium exterius, per viam ducentem ad aquilonem,
And he led me into the outer court by the way that leads to the north,
et introduxit me in gazophylacium quod erat contra separatum ædificium,
and he led me into the storeroom that was opposite the separate edifice,
et contra ædem vergentem ad aquilonem.
and opposite the shrine that verges toward the north.
In facie longitudinis, centum cubitos ostii aquilonis,
The length of the face of the north gate was one hundred cubits,
et latitudinis quinquaginta cubitos,
and the width was fifty cubits.
contra viginti cubitos atrii interioris,
Opposite the twenty cubits of the interior court,
et contra pavimentum stratum lapide atrii exterioris,
and opposite the layer of pavement stones in the outer court,
ubi erat porticus juncta porticui triplici.
in that place, there was a portico joined to a triple portico.
Et ante gazophylacia deambulatio decem cubitorum latitudinis,
And before the storerooms, there was a walkway of ten cubits in width,
ad interiora respiciens viæ cubiti unius.
looking toward the interior along a way of one cubit.
Et ostia eorum ad aquilonem:
And their doors were toward the north.
ubi erant gazophylacia in superioribus humiliora,
In that place, there were storerooms in the upper part of the lower level.
quia supportabant porticus quæ ex illis eminebant de inferioribus,
For they supported the porticos, which projected from them out of the lower level,
et de mediis ædificii.
and out of the middle of the building.
Tristega enim erant,
For they were of three levels,
et non habebant columnas,
and they did not have pillars,
sicut erant columnæ atriorum:
as they were like the pillars of the courts. Because of this,
propterea eminebant de inferioribus, et de mediis a terra cubitis quinquaginta.
they projected from the lower levels and from the middle, fifty cubits from the ground.
Et peribolus exterior secundum gazophylacia,
And the exterior enclosing wall,
quæ erant in via atrii exterioris ante gazophylacia:
adjacent to the storerooms that were along the way of the exterior court in front of the storerooms,
longitudo ejus quinquaginta cubitorum:
was fifty cubits long.
quia longitudo erat gazophylaciorum atrii exterioris quinquaginta cubitorum,
For the length of the storerooms of the exterior court was fifty cubits,
et longitudo ante faciem templi, centum cubitorum.
and the length before the face of the temple was one hundred cubits.
Et erat subter gazophylacia hæc introitus ab oriente,
And under these storerooms, there was an entrance from the east,
ingredientium in ea de atrio exteriori.
for those who were entering into it from the outer court.
In latitudine periboli atrii quod erat contra viam orientalem,
In the width of the enclosing wall of the court that was opposite the way of the east,
in faciem ædificii separati,
at the face of the separate edifice,
et erant ante ædificium gazophylacia.
there were also storerooms, before the edifice.
Et via ante faciem eorum, juxta similitudinem gazophylaciorum quæ erant in via aquilonis:
And the way before their face was in accord with the form of the storerooms which were along the way of the north.
secundum longitudinem eorum,
As was their length,
sic et latitudo eorum,
so also was their width.
et omnis introitus eorum,
And the entire entrance,
et similitudines,
and the likenesses,
et ostia eorum.
and their doors
Secundum ostia gazophylaciorum,
were in accord with the doors of the storerooms that were on the way looking toward the Renown.
quæ erant in via respiciente ad notum:
There was a door at the head of the way,
ostium in capite viæ,
and the way was before a separate vestibule,
quæ via erat ante vestibulum separatum per viam orientalem ingredientibus.
along the way entering toward the east.
Et dixit ad me:
And he said to me:
Gazophylacia aquilonis,
“The storerooms of the north,
et gazophylacia austri,
and the storerooms of the south,
quæ sunt ante ædificium separatum,
which are before the separate edifice,
hæc sunt gazophylacia sancta,
these are holy storerooms,
in quibus vescuntur sacerdotes qui appropinquant ad Dominum in Sancta sanctorum:
in which the priests, who draw near to the Lord in the Holy of Holies, shall eat.
ibi ponent Sancta sanctorum et oblationem pro peccato et pro delicto:
There they shall station the Holy of Holies, and the offering for sin, and for trespasses.
locus enim sanctus est.
For it is a holy place.
Cum autem ingressi fuerint sacerdotes,
And when the priests will have entered,
non egredientur de sanctis in atrium exterius:
they shall not depart from the holy places into the outer court.
et ibi reponent vestimenta sua in quibus ministrant,
And in that place, they shall set their vestments, in which they minister,
quia sancta sunt,
for they are holy.
vestienturque vestimentis aliis:
And they shall be clothed with other vestments,
et sic procedent ad populum.
and in this manner they shall go forth to the people.”
Cumque complesset mensuras domus interioris,
And when he had completed measuring the inner house,
eduxit me per viam portæ quæ respiciebat ad viam orientalem:
he led me out along the way of the gate that looked toward the way of the east.
et mensus est eam undique per circuitum.
And he measured it on every side all around.
Mensus est autem contra ventum orientalem calamo mensuræ,
Then he measured facing the east wind with the measuring reed:
quingentos calamos in calamo mensuræ per circuitum.
five hundred reeds with the measuring reed throughout the course.
Et mensus est contra ventum aquilonis quingentos calamos in calamo mensuræ per gyrum.
And he measured facing the wind of the north: five hundred reeds with the measuring reed throughout the course.
Et ad ventum australem mensus est quingentos calamos in calamo mensuræ per circuitum.
And toward the south wind, he measured five hundred reeds with the measuring reed throughout the course.
Et ad ventum occidentalem mensus est quingentos calamos in calamo mensuræ.
And toward the west wind, he measured five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.
Per quatuor ventos mensus est murum ejus undique per circuitum,
By the four winds,
longitudinem quingentorum cubitorum,
he measured its wall,
et latitudinem quingentorum cubitorum,
on every side throughout the course:
dividentem inter sanctuarium
five hundred cubits in length and five hundred cubits in width,
et vulgi locum.
dividing between the sanctuary and the place of the common people.
